newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy employers chief sees lira/mark rate too high.
newsitem.headline: Italy employers chief sees lira/mark rate too high.

text.p: Giorgio Fossa, chairman of the Italian employers body Confindustria, said he believed the lira's current rate against the German mark was too strong.
"I think the lira's quoted rate is a bit artificial," he told reporters while attending a business meeting.
"A rate of around 990-995 lire against the mark would be difficult for us," he added.
On Thursday afternoon the currently surging lira set a new two-year high against the mark at a quoted 989.80.
Fossa said it was logical international investors should speculate on the lira given Italy's high interest rates.
"We must get interest rates down to bring the lira to a more genuine level," he said.

Structural measures were probably needed to reduce borrowing costs. "Measures contained in the 1997 budget, which are important but not structural, do not give the Bank of Italy enough leverage to further reduce the discount rate without sparking off inflation again." he said.
The central bank cut its key rate in July to 8.25 percent after keeping it at 9.0 percent since May 1995.
